s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral nasal obstruction with purulent discharge and facial pain
salient_findings: Markedly hypertrophic left middle turbinate with granulomatous mucosa
Complete opacification of the ipsilateral maxillary, ethmoid, and frontal sinuses
key_facts: 55-year-old woman
History of diabetes mellitus
3-month history of left-sided nasal obstruction
Purulent nasal discharge
Facial pain
No improvement after multiple courses of oral antibiotics
No recent dental procedures or facial trauma
Anterior rhinoscopic examination showed purulent rhinorrhea
Hypertrophic left middle turbinate with granulomatous mucosa
Noncontrast computed tomography of the paranasal sinuses revealed a heterogeneous, focally hyperdense lesion

shortlist.label: Chronic invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of diabetes mellitus and presents with chronic unilateral nasal obstruction, purulent discharge, and facial pain, which are consistent with chronic invasive fungal sinusitis

shortlist.label: Allergic fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and findings, including hypertrophic left middle turbinate with granulomatous mucosa, are consistent with allergic fungal sinusitis

shortlist.label: Acute invasive fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and findings, including purulent rhinorrhea and a heterogeneous, focally hyperdense lesion on CT, are consistent with acute invasive fungal sinusitis

shortlist.label: Mucormycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of diabetes mellitus, which is a risk factor for mucormycosis, and presents with symptoms consistent with this disease

shortlist.label: Aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms and findings, including chronic unilateral nasal obstruction and purulent discharge, are consistent with aspergillosis

raw.rationale: The patient's 3-month history of symptoms, lack of improvement with antibiotics, and presence of a heterogeneous, focally hyperdense lesion with granulomatous mucosa are consistent with chronic invasive fungal sinusitis, which is also more likely in an immunocompromised patient with a history of diabetes mellitus.

rejected.label: Acute invasive fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The 3-month duration of symptoms is more suggestive of a chronic rather than acute process.

rejected.label: Allergic fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The presence of purulent nasal discharge and granulomatous mucosa is not typical of allergic fungal sinusitis, which usually presents with thick, eosinophilic mucin.

rejected.label: Mucormycosis
rejected.why: Mucormycosis is a more aggressive infection that often presents with bony erosion and necrosis, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Aspergillosis
rejected.why: While aspergillosis can cause chronic invasive fungal sinusitis, the diagnosis is too specific and not directly supported by the provided information, which points more towards a general diagnosis of chronic invasive fungal sinusitis.
